scenes.heading: How ionic bonding works
scenes.narration: Ionic bonding is one of the most important ways that chemical compounds are held together, and understanding it explains a great many everyday materials that you already know.

scenes.heading: Metals give electrons away
scenes.narration: A metal atom holds its outermost electrons loosely, so it can hand one or more of them over to a hungry partner, and it becomes a positively charged particle when it does.

scenes.heading: Building the lattice
scenes.narration: Once the charges exist, opposite charges pull on each other from every direction at once, so the particles stack into a rigid repeating three dimensional lattice rather than separate units.

scenes.heading: Properties of the lattice
scenes.narration: That lattice is strong, so these compounds need very high melting points before they break apart, and they only conduct electricity once they are molten or fully dissolved in water.

scenes.heading: Ionic bonding recap
scenes.narration: So an ionic compound like sodium chloride forms when a metal hands its electrons to a nonmetal, charged particles attract from all directions, and the resulting lattice melts at a very high temperature.
